stem:
The draft financial statements of Bulawayo Joinery Ltd for the year ended 31 December 2025 show: profit for the year US\$96,400; property, plant and equipment US\$410,000; current assets US\$188,000 (including inventory at cost and trade receivables); current liabilities US\$94,000. The draft includes an intangible asset of US\$17,400 (see item 5). Ignore taxation.

| No. | Information found after the draft was prepared |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Inventory includes timber which cost US\$14,800. After the year end it was sold for a net US\$9,350. |
| 2 | A machine cost US\$126,000 and was depreciated over 10 years. After 3 years the total life was reassessed at 15 years. The draft still charged US\$12,600 for 2025. |
| 3 | On 14 January 2026 a customer who owed US\$6,800 at the year end was declared insolvent. |
| 4 | Repairs of US\$4,200 to a vehicle were added to its cost. Vehicles are depreciated at 25% of cost and the draft included a full year's charge on the repairs. |
| 5 | Research costs of US\$17,400 were recorded as an intangible asset. |
| 6 | A machine with a carrying amount of US\$62,000 has a fair value less costs of disposal of US\$48,000 and a value in use of US\$53,500. |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Amounts to be corrected.

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: Calculate the write-down of inventory required by IAS 2 (item 1).

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: Calculate the annual depreciation of the machine in item 2 under the revised life.
parts.explanation: Carrying amount 126,000 - 3 × 12,600 = 88,200; remaining life 12 years; 88,200 ÷ 12 = 7,350.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.stem: Calculate the impairment loss in item 6.
parts.explanation: Recoverable amount = higher of 48,000 and 53,500 = 53,500; loss = 62,000 - 53,500 = 8,500.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Recoverable amount = higher of 48,000 and 53,500 = 53,500; loss = 62,000 - 53,500 = 8,500.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the corrected profit for the year after all six items.
parts.explanation: 96,400 - inventory 5,450 + depreciation saved 5,250 - irrecoverable debt 6,800 - repairs 4,200 + depreciation reversed 1,050 - research 17,400 - impairment 8,500 = 60,350.
parts.workedSolution: 1. 96,400 - inventory 5,450 + depreciation saved 5,250 - irrecoverable debt 6,800 - repairs 4,200 + depreciation reversed 1,050 - research 17,400 - impairment 8,500 = 60,350.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the corrected carrying amount of property, plant and equipment.
parts.explanation: 410,000 + depreciation saved 5,250 - repairs net of depreciation 3,150 - impairment 8,500 = 403,600.
parts.workedSolution: 1. 410,000 + depreciation saved 5,250 - repairs net of depreciation 3,150 - impairment 8,500 = 403,600.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the corrected current ratio, as x : 1 to two decimal places.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: For items 1 to 6, state the standard that applies and the type of matter (adjusting event, change in estimate, or correction of a presentation or measurement rule).

points.description: Item 1: IAS 2 (lower of cost and NRV), supported by an adjusting event after the year end
Item 2: IAS 8 (change in accounting estimate, applied prospectively) with IAS 16 depreciation
Items 3 and 4: item 3 is an adjusting event (IAS 10); item 4 is IAS 16 (repairs are not part of cost)
Items 5 and 6: item 5 is IAS 38 (research is expensed); item 6 is IAS 36 (impairment to recoverable amount)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Item 1: IAS 2, with an adjusting event. Item 2: IAS 8, a change in estimate. Item 3: IAS 10, adjusting event. Item 4: IAS 16, repairs are expenses. Item 5: IAS 38, research is expensed. Item 6: IAS 36, impairment.

parts.explanation: One mark for each pair of items correctly classified.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: The directors prefer to publish the draft profit of US\$96,400. Evaluate their preference and advise them.

points.description: The corrected profit is 60,350, 36,050 lower (37.40% of the draft), so the draft overstates profit
Items 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6 reduce profit because the standards require losses to be recognised, and only item 2 raises profit, as a change in estimate
The current ratio falls from 2 : 1 to 1.87 : 1, so liquidity is weaker than the draft shows
Using the draft would breach IAS 1 (fair presentation) and mislead users such as lenders and shareholders
Advice: adopt the corrected figures, disclose the change in estimate and the impairment in the notes, and explain the changes to the users

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The corrected profit of 60,350 is well below the draft of 96,400, and the current ratio falls from 2 to 1.87. Publishing the draft would breach fair presentation and mislead users. The directors should adopt the corrected figures and disclose the changes.

parts.explanation: One mark each for the profit difference, the effect of the standards, liquidity, the breach of fair presentation and the advice.

explanation: This item applies IAS 2, IAS 8, IAS 10, IAS 16, IAS 36 and IAS 38 to correct a draft set of statements and evaluates the effect.
hints: Adjusting events change the figures; the estimate is prospective.

stem:
Harare Household Supplies has three departments: furniture, kitchenware and gifts. The figures for the year ended 31 December 2025 are below. Wages of each department's own staff are allocated directly.

|  | Furniture US\$ | Kitchenware US\$ | Gifts US\$ |

| Opening inventory | 18,350 | 9,640 | 5,180 |
| Purchases | 72,480 | 43,150 | 20,370 |
| Closing inventory | 19,720 | 10,280 | 5,010 |
| Departmental wages | 12,430 | 7,860 | 5,640 |

Common expenses and income.

| Item | US\$ | Basis of apportionment |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Rent | 16,800 | Floor area (140 : 85 : 55 m²) |
| Lighting and heating | 4,200 | Floor area |
| General wages | 17,500 | Number of staff (5 : 3 : 2) |
| Advertising | 6,900 | Sales |
| Depreciation | 6,400 | Asset values (22,000 : 14,000 : 4,000) |
| Commission received (income) | 2,300 | Sales |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Apportionment and trading results.

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: Calculate the rent charged to the gifts department.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: Calculate the cost of sales of the furniture department.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.stem: Calculate the gross profit of the kitchenware department.

parts.label: (b)

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: Furniture.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: Kitchenware.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.stem: Gifts.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: The gifts department would be closed. Only its own wages would be saved and the common expenses would continue. Calculate the contribution of the gifts department.
parts.explanation: Gross profit 12,960 + commission 335 - own wages 5,640 = 7,655.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Prepare the departmental statement of profit or loss for the year ended 31 December 2025, with a total column.

points.description: Three-line heading and the three department columns with a total column
Revenue, cost of sales and gross profit of each department
Commission received and the expenses, allocated and apportioned
Net profit or loss of each department and total net profit 20,410

parts.explanation: One mark for each element; allow follow-through.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Evaluate the proposal to close the gifts department and advise the owner.

points.description: Gifts shows a loss of 1,615, but it contributes 7,655 towards the common costs
If it closed, total net profit would fall from 20,410 to 12,755, because the common costs would continue
Advice: keep the department, review its margin and the floor area it uses, and close it only if the space could earn more elsewhere

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Gifts shows a loss of 1,615 but contributes 7,655. Closing it would reduce total net profit to 12,755. The owner should keep it, review its margin and use of space, and close it only if the space can earn more.

parts.explanation: One mark for the contribution, one for the effect on total profit and one for the advice.

explanation: This item tests the apportionment of common expenses, the departmental statement of profit or loss and the closure decision.
hints: Apportion on the basis shown for each expense.
The contribution ignores the common costs that continue.
